title: Next Warmer Day
statement: A weather station recorded one temperature per day. For each day, find how many days you would have to wait for a strictly warmer temperature.
If no later day is strictly warmer, the answer for that day is `0`.
inputFormat: The first line contains an integer `n`.
The second line contains `n` integers, the temperatures in order.
outputFormat: Print `n` integers separated by spaces. The `i`-th integer is `j - i` for the smallest `j > i` with `t[j] > t[i]`, or `0` if there is no such day.
constraints: The output has up to 200000 numbers; build it in one string instead of printing each number separately.

examples.explanation: Equal temperatures are not warmer, so day 0 waits two days for 72.
Each day is followed by a warmer one, except the last.

starter.output: n integers separated by spaces: days to wait for a strictly warmer day, or 0

private.complexity: O(n) with a stack of indices whose temperatures are decreasing. Scanning forward from every day is O(n^2) and times out on the long-delay hidden case.
private.notes: Pop while t[stack.top] < t[i] (strict), so equal temperatures stay on the stack.
